help_articles.title: Filter Operations Overview
help_articles.content:
# Filter Operations Overview

The Filter Operations page is the central hub for managing filter cleaning cycles. Operators use this page to move filters through their cleaning lifecycle stages.

## Key Concepts

- **Stages**: Filters progress through stages like Wash In, Wash Out, Dry In, Dry Out, Storage In, Storage Out
- **Blocks**: Filters are assigned to cleaning blocks/areas before operations
- **Scanning**: Filters are identified by scanning QR codes or entering filter names
- **Cleaning Reasons**: Each cycle requires a reason (PM, Type-C, etc.)

## Workflow

1. Select a cleaning stage (e.g., Wash In)
2. Select the block/cleaning area
3. Scan or enter the filter identifier
4. If starting a new cycle, select the cleaning reason
5. If equipment groups are configured, select readings
6. Complete any required checklists

## Stage Flow

Filters follow the pipeline defined in their assigned Cleaning Profile. The system enforces stage order and blocks advancement until checklists are completed.

help_articles.title: Filter Scanning & Identification
help_articles.content:
# Filter Scanning & Identification

Filters can be identified in multiple ways during operations:

## QR Code Scanning
- Use the device camera to scan the QR code on the filter
- QR codes are generated from the Entity > QR Code tab
- Scanning automatically looks up the filter by its identifier

## Manual Entry
- Type the filter name (e.g., HEPA-A-001)
- The system performs a case-insensitive name match

## Identifier Lookup
- Filters with registered identifiers (QR, RFID, NFC) are resolved automatically
- The lookup checks the asset identifiers table first, then falls back to name matching

help_articles.title: Equipment Groups & Instrument Readings
help_articles.content:
# Equipment Groups & Instrument Readings

Equipment groups link measuring instruments to cleaning blocks for recording pressure and temperature readings during filter operations.

## Setup
1. Go to Configuration > Equipment Groups
2. Select a Block
3. Create a group with 3 instruments:
   - Compressed Air Pressure (Wash In stage)
   - RO Water Pressure (Wash In stage)
   - Dryer Temperature (Dry In stage)

## Recording Readings
- During Wash In: Select equipment group, then choose pressure values from dropdowns
- During Dry In: Record dryer temperature reading
- Dropdown values are generated from operating range and least count

## Instrument Configuration
- **Instrument Range**: Full measurement range of the instrument
- **Operating Range**: Acceptable operating values (subset of instrument range)
- **Least Count**: Smallest measurable increment (determines dropdown step size)
- **UOM**: Unit of measurement (bar, °C, etc.)

help_articles.title: Cleaning Cycle History
help_articles.content:
# Cleaning Cycle History

The Cleaning Cycles page shows a complete history of all filter cleaning operations.

## Cycle Information
- **Cycle Code**: Unique identifier (format: CC-ORG-FILTER-SEQ-DATE)
- **Status**: In Progress, Completed, or Terminated
- **Progress**: Visual indicators showing completed stages
- **Duration**: Total time from start to completion

## Filtering
Filter cycles by status using the tabs: All, In Progress, Completed, Terminated.

## Expanded View
Click any cycle to expand and see the stage-by-stage timeline with:
- Stage transitions with timestamps
- Performer names
- Remarks and justifications
- Instrument readings

## Cycle Detail
Click "View" to see the full timeline with all events, checklists, and deviations.

help_articles.title: Cycle Timeline & Events
help_articles.content:
# Cycle Timeline & Events

The cycle detail page shows every event that occurred during a cleaning cycle.

## Event Types
- **CYCLE_STARTED**: Cycle initiated with cleaning reason
- **STATE_TRANSITION**: Filter moved to next stage
- **CHECKLIST_COMPLETED**: Required checklist answered
- **PARAMETER_CAPTURE**: Instrument readings recorded
- **BYPASS_DEVIATION**: Stage was bypassed (deviation logged)
- **CYCLE_COMPLETED**: All stages finished successfully

## Instrument Readings
Readings are displayed with instrument description, value, and unit. These are recorded during Wash In (pressure) and Dry In (temperature) stages.

## Deviations
If a stage is bypassed, the deviation justification is displayed with a red indicator.

help_articles.title: Cleaning Profiles Overview
help_articles.content:
# Cleaning Profiles Overview

Cleaning Profiles define the pipeline of stages and checklists that filters must follow during cleaning operations.

## Profile Structure
A cleaning profile is a directed graph of nodes:
- **START**: Entry point (required)
- **END**: Exit point (required)
- **STAGE**: Cleaning stage (Wash In, Wash Out, Dry In, etc.)
- **CHECKLIST**: Required survey/checklist between stages

## Flow Modes
- **STRICT**: Stages must be followed in exact order
- **BYPASS_ENABLED**: Operators can skip stages with justification

## Versioning
Profiles are versioned. When updated, a new version is created and all assigned filters are migrated to the new version. Old versions are archived.

## Profile Examples
- **Full Cycle**: All stages with checklists at every transition
- **Quick Wash**: Wash only with post-wash checklist
- **Wash and Dry**: No storage phase
- **Dry and Store**: For pre-washed filters

help_articles.title: Pipeline Visual Editor
help_articles.content:
# Pipeline Visual Editor

The visual editor lets you design cleaning pipelines by placing and connecting nodes on a canvas.

## Adding Nodes
1. Click the node type button in the toolbar (Stage, Checklist, etc.)
2. The node appears on the canvas
3. Configure the node in the properties panel

## Connecting Nodes
1. Drag from an output port (right side) to an input port (left side)
2. Connections define the flow order

## Node Configuration
- **STAGE nodes**: Select the stage key (WASH_IN, DRY_OUT, etc.)
- **CHECKLIST nodes**: Select which checklist profile to use

## Validation Rules
- Must have exactly 1 START and 1 END node
- START must have at least 1 outgoing connection
- END must have at least 1 incoming connection
- All STAGE nodes need a stage key assigned
- All CHECKLIST nodes need a checklist profile assigned
- No disconnected nodes allowed

help_articles.title: Checklist Profiles Guide
help_articles.content:
# Checklist Profiles Guide

Checklist Profiles are reusable survey templates attached to cleaning pipeline nodes. When a filter reaches a CHECKLIST node, the operator must answer all required questions before advancing.

## Question Types
- **YES/NO**: Simple yes or no answer
- **YES/NO/NA**: Yes, No, or Not Applicable
- **PASS/FAIL**: Pass or fail assessment
- **TEXT**: Free-form text input
- **NUMERIC**: Number with min/max validation and unit
- **DROPDOWN**: Select from predefined options
- **MULTI_SELECT**: Select multiple options

## Creating a Checklist
1. Go to Checklists page
2. Click "Create Checklist Profile"
3. Add questions with type, section, and validation
4. Reorder questions as needed

## Sections
Group related questions under sections for better organization. Section headers appear automatically in the checklist dialog.

## Attaching to Pipeline
In the Cleaning Profile editor, add a CHECKLIST node and select this profile from the dropdown.

help_articles.title: Filter Profile Assignment
help_articles.content:
# Filter Profile Assignment

Filter Profiles link individual filter entities to their cleaning profile, determining which pipeline they follow during operations.

## Assigning a Profile
1. Go to Filter Profiles page
2. Select a filter entity
3. Choose a cleaning profile to assign
4. The filter will follow that profile's pipeline during cleaning cycles

## Bulk Assignment
From the Cleaning Profiles page, use "Assign Assets" to assign the profile to multiple filters at once.

## Profile Changes
When a cleaning profile is updated (new version), all filters assigned to it are automatically migrated to the new version.

help_articles.title: Equipment Groups Configuration
help_articles.content:
# Equipment Groups Configuration

Equipment Groups define the instruments used during filter cleaning operations. Each group contains 3 mandatory instruments.

## Instruments
1. **Compressed Air Pressure** (Wash In stage) — measures air pressure in bar
2. **RO Water Pressure** (Wash In stage) — measures water pressure in bar
3. **Dryer Temperature** (Dry In stage) — measures dryer temperature in °C

## Configuration Fields
- **S.No**: Serial number of the instrument
- **Instrument ID**: Unique identifier code
- **UOM**: Unit of measurement
- **Instrument Range**: Full measurement range (min-max)
- **Operating Range**: Acceptable operating values
- **Least Count**: Smallest measurable increment

## Block Assignment
Each equipment group belongs to a Block (cleaning area). Select the block first, then create/manage groups for that block.

help_articles.title: PM Schedule Management
help_articles.content:
# PM Schedule Management

Preventive Maintenance (PM) Schedules automate the scheduling of filter cleaning based on time intervals.

## Creating a Schedule
1. Navigate to PM Schedules
2. Select an entity (filter or equipment)
3. Set the interval in days
4. Define the maintenance window

## Schedule Execution
- When a PM is due, it appears in the upcoming executions list
- Completing a PM execution records the event and schedules the next occurrence
- Overdue PMs are highlighted for attention

## PM vs Manual Cleaning
- PM cleaning uses the reason code "PM"
- Manual cleaning uses other reason codes (Type-C, On Request, etc.)
- Both follow the same cleaning profile pipeline

help_articles.title: Filter Lifecycle States
help_articles.content:
# Filter Lifecycle States

Filter lifecycle states track the current condition and location of each filter in the system.

## Default States
- **New**: Filter not yet used
- **Installed**: Filter installed in AHU
- **Ready for Use**: Filter cleaned and ready
- **In Use**: Filter actively in use
- **Wash In/Out**: Filter in washing process
- **Dry In/Out**: Filter in drying process
- **Storage In/Out**: Filter in storage
- **Retired**: Filter end of life
- **Damaged**: Filter damaged

## State Transitions
State transitions are controlled by the cleaning profile pipeline. The system enforces valid transitions and blocks invalid ones.

## Configuration
Customize lifecycle states in Configuration > Filter Lifecycle States. Add, edit, or disable states as needed.
